rule_name: Crush garlic and rest before heating

action.description: Crush or mince; rest about 10 minutes before heating
action.engine_instruction: When garlic is cooked, place crushing/mincing before a short rest, then add later or cook gently.

evidence.summary: Controlled food-processing studies show crushing before heating preserves more thiosulfinate-forming potential than heating intact garlic.

sources.title: Heating garlic inhibits its anticancer properties

action.description: Cook/chop tomato and include a modest amount of culinary oil
action.engine_instruction: For tomato sauces or soups, cook tomatoes and retain/add an unsaturated culinary oil.

evidence.summary: Human feeding studies show processed tomato with oil increases circulating carotenoid response.

sources.title: Processed tomato products and dietary lipids increase lycopene bioavailability

action.description: Cook until tender; chop, mash, or puree
action.engine_instruction: For carotenoid optimization, prefer cooked chopped/pureed carrots over intact raw pieces.

evidence.summary: Human and in-vitro digestion studies support greater carotenoid bioaccessibility from processed plant matrices.

sources.title: Effect of food matrix and processing on carotenoid bioavailability

action.description: Cook or finely chop; serve with fat
action.engine_instruction: For carotenoid-focused recipes, use cooked or finely chopped greens and apply the fat-pairing rule.

evidence.summary: Food-matrix research supports greater carotenoid release after processing, with preparation-specific variation.

rule_name: Add active myrosinase to cooked crucifers

action.description: Add mustard powder or a small amount of raw crucifer after cooking
action.engine_instruction: If crucifers are cooked thoroughly, suggest mustard powder as a finishing ingredient when compatible.

evidence.summary: Human feeding work shows mustard seed powder increases sulforaphane bioavailability from cooked broccoli.

sources.title: Mustard seed powder increases bioavailability of sulforaphane in cooked broccoli

action.description: Chop and allow a short rest before applying high heat
action.engine_instruction: Schedule chopping before other prep; use brief steaming when feasible.

evidence.summary: Mechanistic and food-processing studies support pre-chopping and gentler cooking to preserve myrosinase activity.

sources.title: Effects of processing on glucosinolates and myrosinase

action.description: Soak when appropriate, discard soak water, and cook fully
action.engine_instruction: For dry legumes, include soaking where culturally and culinarily appropriate; always cook fully.

evidence.summary: Reviews show household processing can reduce phytate, though mineral bioavailability gains vary.

sources.title: Effects of food processing on antinutrients in legumes

action.engine_instruction: When compatible, suggest sourdough/fermented batter rather than unfermented equivalents.

evidence.summary: Human and food-processing literature supports phytate reduction through fermentation.

sources.title: Influence of fermentation on mineral bioavailability

rule_name: Cook eggs rather than consume raw

action.engine_instruction: Never optimize protein absorption by recommending raw egg; retain food-safety cooking guidance.

evidence.summary: Stable-isotope human study found substantially greater digestibility of cooked versus raw egg protein.

sources.title: Digestibility of cooked and raw egg protein in humans

action.engine_instruction: Reject undercooked dry beans; prefer full boiling/pressure cooking.

evidence.summary: Food science evidence shows adequate heat reduces protease inhibitors and improves digestibility; safety evidence is strong.

sources.title: Lectins in dry legumes and safe preparation

action.description: Prefer nixtamalized masa for relevant dishes
action.engine_instruction: For tortillas/tamales, map nixtamalized masa as the preferred corn form when niacin is the target.

evidence.summary: Historical, biochemical, and nutrition evidence establishes nixtamalization as improving niacin availability.

sources.title: Niacin: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

action.description: Use ground rather than whole seeds when nutrient access is the goal
action.engine_instruction: Substitute ground seed for whole seed when texture permits; preserve portion size.

evidence.summary: Human trials show greater uptake of flax components from ground versus whole seed.

sources.title: Bioavailability of alpha-linolenic acid in subjects after ingestion of three different forms of flaxseed

rule_name: Avoid prolonged boiling of water-soluble vitamins

action.description: Use steaming, microwaving, or brief cooking with minimal water
action.engine_instruction: When vitamin C or folate is the target, prefer brief low-water methods or retain cooking liquid in the dish.

evidence.summary: USDA nutrient-retention research and reviews support method-dependent losses of water-soluble vitamins.

sources.title: USDA Table of Nutrient Retention Factors
